X: States a single $100 pair does not qualify for free shipping; the site's threshold is $100 and the Tree Runner NZ page shows a '+ Free shipping' badge, so this is likely wrong (not invented, but a misread)
Y: 'Sugarcane-based sole' and 'Sugarcane sole' headline: only the SweetFoam midsole is sugarcane-based, not the whole sole
Soda can weight given as a 'working figure (about 13 oz)', not sourced
Z: 'Allbirds began in New Zealand with Tim Brown' simplifies the founding (company started in San Francisco with co-founder Joey Zwillinger); defensible as brand-roots story but a stretch
'83 active US ads' in the Ad Library could not be verified by me

reasons: Live checks on allbirds.com (10 Nov 2026) confirmed most core facts in all three: Tree Runner $100, Final Few badge, 8.6 oz M9, TENCEL Lyocell + recycled polyester upper, SweetFoam midsole, merino-blend lining, recycled-bottle laces, machine washable with insoles hand-washed, Conde Nast Traveler quote, 4.6 stars / 9,951 reviews; Tree Runner NZ $100, 8.9 oz, Featherbed insole, true to size, 'latest iteration of our fan-fave Tree Runner', broad size run in stock. Z made the decisive media-buyer call to land cold traffic on the in-stock NZ, re-grounded every number to that product, attributed the quote honestly to the original, added description field, character counts and test hypotheses. X has the strongest copy craft and accurate stock table but leaves the stock problem as a three-way choice and misreads free shipping. Y is accurate on stock (sizes 11-14 gone) yet still sends all five ads to that page, its rating ad is a generic DTC angle, and 'sugarcane sole' overstates the material.

biggest_flaw.X: Does not decide where to send traffic even though the hero product is nearly sold out; the client must choose among three options before anything can run.
biggest_flaw.Y: Points every ad at the Final Few Tree Runner page where sizes 11-14 are sold out in every colour, so cold clicks will often fail to convert.
biggest_flaw.Z: The wash concept's primary text never names the product or price, and the founder story ('began in New Zealand') is a slight simplification.

best_thing.X: Tight, specific, on-brand copy with designer guardrails (no tumble dryer, Green Guides wording rules, accuracy rule for the scale) and a full claim-to-source table.
best_thing.Y: Short, clean, verifiable copy with a well-checked stock warning and a real, current rating/review count used as social proof.
best_thing.Z: Switches the landing page to the in-stock, true-to-size Tree Runner NZ and rebuilds all claims (8.9 oz, Featherbed insole, free shipping) around it, with ranked concepts, test hypotheses and character counts.
